question: Should the bounded-map work be combined with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100176, or should maintainers select an explicit landing and rebase order for the two breaker-lifecycle changes?
rationale: Both branches modify the same state-machine functions with interacting retention semantics, and code inspection cannot determine the preferred integration strategy without owner intent.

options.title: Combine the lifecycle changes
options.body: Integrate bounded retention and half-open probing into one reviewed state model with shared regression and runtime proof.

options.title: Land the bound first
options.body: Merge this PR after real proof, then rebase the half-open work onto the bounded implementation.

options.title: Land half-open first
options.body: Merge the retained-state behavior first, then revise this PR’s expiry and eviction rules against that model.

recommendation.title: Combine the lifecycle changes
recommendation.body: Integrate bounded retention and half-open probing into one reviewed state model with shared regression and runtime proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced Active Memory and carried several major recall and configuration changes, providing the strongest area-level context for choosing the final lifecycle.
